headline: High: shared file-based workflows and broad network/MCP surfaces create default risks of leakage, conflict, and cascading misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ms-swift reads/writes files and uses stdin/stdout, while next-ai-draw-io accepts natural-language commands and MCP-backed inputs. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content from one agent be treated as instructions by the other. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF both agents are connected through a shared filesystem or copied text channel, prompt-like content can cross from one to the other.
IF next-ai-draw-io ingests MCP or document text without provenance checks, injected instructions can be followed.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and disable shared folders.
Strip instructions from imported text before passing between agents.
Require a human approval step for any cross-agent prompt content.
Use provenance labels on files and messages.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch files and sensitive operational data classes: ms-swift handles datasets, checkpoints, logs, and secrets; next-ai-draw-io processes PDFs, text, and images and requests API keys. If they share a workspace or the same account context, file contents can flow into broad network egress paths. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default-style deployments, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF the two agents share a directory containing datasets, logs, PDFs, or diagrams, one agent can read the other's sensitive files.
IF either agent is configured with the same API key or token store, secrets may be exposed across tasks.
mitigations: Use separate OS users and separate workspaces.
Move secrets out of shared directories.
Disable automatic file import from shared folders.
Rotate any API keys used by next-ai-draw-io.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and secret scoping.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ms-swift can write the filesystem, execute shell commands, and spawn subprocesses; next-ai-draw-io has broad network egress and browser/MCP access. Even without explicit git overlap, both can mutate shared resources if pointed at the same workspace or external service. Because locking and session scope are not stated, uncertainty favors medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are given write access to the same directory, they can overwrite each other's files.
IF both agents target the same external API or MCP resource, concurrent mutations can race.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Serialize writes with a simple manual lock file.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same remote resource.
Check for stale outputs before saving.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking and resource arbitration.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ms-swift can generate training, evaluation, and configuration outputs, and next-ai-draw-io is a document-processing assistant that can turn inputs into visual artifacts. If next-ai-draw-io treats ms-swift outputs as authoritative, errors can propagate into diagrams or downstream actions. No verification workflow is documented, so the cascade is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io consumes ms-swift-generated text or config without review, it may render or act on incorrect facts.
IF ms-swift outputs are copied into diagrams or docs as source of truth, mistakes can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review before reuse of generated outputs.
Mark AI-generated files as untrusted by default.
Compare outputs against source documents before acting.
Keep raw source and derived artifacts in separate folders.
requires-engineering: add verification gates and provenance tracking.

E_compliance.rationale: ms-swift handles hub tokens, SDK tokens, datasets, checkpoints, and logs; next-ai-draw-io handles API keys and broad cloud model endpoints. If regulated or customer data is processed, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches across two different open-source stacks. The profiles do not state certifications or residency controls, so uncertainty again favors medium.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is placed into both tools, their separate logging and retention behaviors may diverge.
IF EU or PHI data is sent through next-ai-draw-io's external model endpoints, residency or certification requirements may be violated.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to either tool until policies are confirmed.
Document retention settings for logs and outputs.
Use region-restricted endpoints where available.
Store secrets in a dedicated vault, not in app configs.
requires-engineering: obtain vendor compliance attestations and enforce policy controls.
